rows.parameter: [1. OPERATING EMPTY WEIGHT -- THE HEADLINE. Expected = Brandt Wt!B12 = 19,980.70; Alt = corrections.xls 19,148.08]

rows.Notes: Statistical empty-weight power law We/Wto = Kvs*A*W_TO^C, A = 2.34 / C = -0.13 [metabook_data.md:22]. A CENTRAL regression through historical fighters, so a few percent is the expected accuracy -- and it happens to land closest to Brandt of anything in this report.

DIFFERENT KIND OF QUANTITY: a LOWER BOUND (the historical efficiency frontier), not a central estimate. Any real OEW must sit ABOVE it, so a negative %Diff is the CORRECT result and its magnitude is not an error measure. Never summed into OEW.

rows.parameter: OEW, Tbl 15.2 psf buildup + Raymer W_en [lbf]
rows.Notes: OFFICIAL L2. wing 9 / HT 4 / VT 5.3 psf on EXPOSED planform + fuselage 4.8 psf on WETTED area [Raymer Tbl 15.2] + LG 0.033*W_TO, installed engine 1.3 x bare, all-else 0.17*W_TO [AE481 metabook Sec. 7]. Of the gap to Brandt, 2733.68 lbf (13.68 % of Wt!B12) is Brandt components with NO framework analog -- see section 5.

rows.parameter: OEW, Tbl 15.2 psf buildup + Brandt W_en alt [lbf]
rows.Notes: Same buildup with Brandt's own already-installed 0.199*T_AB engine weight substituted (NO x1.3). A different engine-model FAMILY, so the framework is expected to differ; reported because engine weight is the single largest divergence at L2.

rows.parameter: OEW, Tbl 15.2 psf + Brandt W_en x1.3 -- REJECTED [lbf]
rows.Notes: REJECTED VARIANT, reported so the decision is auditable. Applies the metabook's x1.3 to a formula readme_wt.md:230 states IS ALREADY the installed-engine weight, i.e. it installs twice. It agrees BEST with Brandt of every L2 option, and that is precisely why it is rejected: agreement produced by a double-counted factor is not agreement. Not a candidate.

OFFICIAL L3, at the settled decisions: UNINSTALLED W_en (no x1.3), W_l = 0.95*W_TO, SFC_mission by DI at the requirements cruise point. Eqs. 15.1-15.24 group mass differently from Brandt's psf model, and the same 2733.68 lbf of unmodelled Brandt components applies.

rows.parameter: OEW, Sec. 15.3.1 with W_en x1.3 -- REJECTED [lbf]
rows.Notes: REJECTED VARIANT, reported so decision 1 is auditable. It is CLOSER to Brandt than the settled answer, because it double-counts the installation hardware Eqs. 15.7-15.15 already supply item by item. The better agreement was the evidence AGAINST x1.3, not for it. x1.3 is L2-only, and L2 has no buildup.

rows.parameter: [2. STRUCTURAL LINE ITEMS -- Brandt Wt!C9:H9. His psf coefficients are Wt!C7:H7 (wing 6.75 / fus 5.0 / pitch 6.0 / VT 6.0), NOT Raymer Tbl 15.2's]

rows.Notes: Framework: 9.0 psf x EXPOSED planform 196.2261 ft^2 [Raymer Tbl 15.2, metabook_data.md:321]. Brandt: 6.75 psf x S_ref with AR^1.8, n_ult^0.2, tc^-0.7 and 1/cos(Lambda) factors -- a psf model like ours but a different coefficient AND different correction factors.

Raymer Eq. 15.1 statistical buildup. Reads ~34 % above Brandt: Raymer's fighter-wing regression is fitted across production aircraft and does not capture the F-16's unusually light, highly optimised wing. Raymer states these are estimates with intrinsic scatter. Every Eq. 15.1 exponent is an OPEN verify-against-book item (todo Sec. 3a).

Framework: 4.8 psf x WETTED area 730.3023 ft^2 [Raymer Tbl 15.2, metabook_data.md:324; area via Roskam Vol. II Eq. 12.3]. Brandt: 5.0 psf x his own S_wet_fuse 730.422 x a fineness factor -- nearly the same area, so this row isolates the psf coefficient difference.

Raymer Eq. 15.4, on the 47.5 ft T.O. length and the 5.0 ft maximum structural DEPTH. ! D_fus here is NOT geom.D_fus = 6.0 (the Roskam equivalent diameter): Eq. 15.4 carries D_fus^0.849, so that substitution would inflate this row by +17.9 % silently.

DIFFERENT AREA CONVENTION, not an agreement check. Brandt Wt!E9 = 6.0 x Main!C18 = 6.0 x 108, the FULL planform; the framework uses the EXPOSED planform per Raymer Tbl 15.2's own definition (49.8473 ft^2 at L2). The Alt column's 199.39 is close only because corrections.xls happens to land near 4.0 x exposed.

Same FULL-vs-EXPOSED definitional split as the L2 row. Raymer Eq. 15.2 on the EXPOSED 51.1486 ft^2, which is +2.605 % above L2's 49.8473 because F16GeomL3 takes the physical 18.5 ft HT span as primary (F16GeomL3.md Sec. A.4) -- itself BY DESIGN, not error.
DIFFERENT AREA CONVENTION. Brandt Wt!F9 = 6.0 x Main!H18 = 6.0 x 60, the FULL planform; the framework uses the EXPOSED 40.8897 ft^2 x 5.3 psf [metabook_data.md:323].

Same FULL-vs-EXPOSED split. Raymer Eq. 15.3 on the EXPOSED planform SET -- S_vt 40.8897, AR_vt 1.294, lambda_vt 0.437 -- NOT the FULL 60 / 1.6 / 0.5. Eq. 15.3 also carries a documented code-vs-extract exponent CONFLICT on cos(Lambda_vt) (todo Sec. 3a row 2).
No framework nacelle-weight component exists at any fidelity level. Brandt: 4.5 psf x his half-buried nacelle area (Geom!B4). Counted in the section-5 gap tally.
No framework strake component exists -- the same gap the geometry report records for strake wetted/exposed area. Brandt: 4.5 psf x 20 ft^2. Counted in the section-5 gap tally.

NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE: Brandt's Wt!B9 = SUM(C9:H9) also contains nacelles (186.82) and strakes (90.00), for which the framework has no analog, and two of the four shared items use his FULL-planform tail areas. Group-level agreement is not meaningful here.
Same non-like-for-like subtotal as the L2 row, over the Sec. 15.3.1 components.

rows.parameter: [3. ENGINE + SYSTEMS -- Brandt Wt!B22:B31. His fraction literals are Wt!F23:F31, live-verified 2026-07-25]

rows.Notes: SAME MODEL FAMILY, different coefficient: framework 0.033*W_TO [AE481 metabook Sec. 7, metabook_data.md:330] vs Brandt 0.034*W_TO (Wt!F23 = 0.034, a bare literal). LOCKED decision (user 2026-07-24): use 0.033. The -2.94 % is exactly 0.033/0.034 - 1, i.e. entirely the coefficient choice.

Brandt carries ONE gear line; the framework splits main (Eq. 15.5) and nose (Eq. 15.6), so only the total below compares. Reported for the breakdown. L_m is converted feet->INCHES per Raymer's nomenclature; omitting that made the gear ~11x too light.
See the main-gear row: Brandt has no nose/main split.

A statistical strut-sizing buildup vs Brandt's 0.034*W_TO fraction -- different formula families, and they agree to within ~9 %. Was 1057.27 (-0.9 %) before Phase 4, on a FROZEN W_l = 20681 [Brandt Wt!B41] that made the entire gear group insensitive to gross weight (todo Sec. P4-17). The apparently better old agreement came from a dead computation.

Different formula families: Raymer Eq. 15.10 on duct geometry (L_d, L_s, D_e) vs Brandt's 3.9 x W_nacelles -- and the framework has no nacelle weight at all, so his basis does not even exist here. Eq. 15.10 is the WEAKEST-SOURCED equation in WeightsL3: three of its terms are FROM-CODE, absent from the repo extract (todo Sec. 3a rows 3-7).

Raymer Eq. 15.17 on M, S_cs, N_s, N_c vs Brandt's 0.012*W_TO + a LE-flap area term. Different families. S_cs = 190 ft^2 is an unpinned geometry estimate, and N_c^0.127 is FROM-CODE (todo Sec. 3a rows 10-13).
Raymer Eq. 15.20 on R_kva, L_a, N_gen vs Brandt's 0.017*W_TO. R_kva = 80 and L_a = 10 ft are unpinned estimates, so this row's agreement is partly a property of those guesses.
Raymer Eq. 15.19 = 37.23*K_vsh*N_u^0.664 vs Brandt's 0.0117*W_TO. N_u = 5 is an unpinned estimate and the equation is very sensitive to it, which is the likely bulk of the gap.
Raymer Eq. 15.23 on the avionics weight and crew count vs Brandt's 0.0115*W_TO.

Raymer Eq. 15.21 = 2.117*W_uav^0.933 vs Brandt's 0.081*W_TO. W_uav = 1500 lbf is an UNPINNED estimate for the Block 10 suite, and it is the only input -- so this row is really a statement about that estimate, not about the equation.

Brandt does not tabulate a fuel-system line. Reported because it is the ONLY consumer of SFC_mission (see section 4b): moving SFC from Brandt's 0.70 to the framework's cruise 1.0071 (+43.87 %) moves this component only +9.48 %, since Eq. 15.16 carries ((T*SFC)/1000)^0.249. V_t = 940 gal rests on an UNCITED 6.7 lb/gal density (todo Sec. P4-5b).

A LUMPED 0.30 x W_structure catch-all with no single framework analog -- whatever it covers is distributed across the framework's named components, or missing. The largest single unmodelled item, 10.09 % of Wt!B12. Counted in the section-5 tally.
No framework analog. Brandt: 0.10 x expendable payload = 0.10 x 4400. Counted in the section-5 tally.

L3 OEW less the whole engine GROUP. Not like-for-like: Brandt's B10 excludes only his single engine line (B11), while the framework's engine group also contains the Eqs. 15.7-15.15 installation hardware, some of which Brandt books under other headings.

W_en UNINSTALLED [Raymer Eq. 10.10] -- OFFICIAL at L3 [lbf]

The x1.3 installed/bare factor [AE481 metabook Sec. 7, metabook_data.md:333] is L2-ONLY -- L2 has no installation buildup, so one lumped factor is the right model there and only there. rows.Notes: EXACT BY CONSTRUCTION -- it IS Brandt's own formula fed Brandt's own thrust. Kept as a POSITIVE CONTROL that the propulsion DI delivers T_SL = 23,770 lbf correctly; a nonzero %Diff here would mean the injected thrust is wrong. Brandt's 0.199 is never ported into a framework equation.

rows.Notes: REJECTED, reported once and labelled. Double-applies an installation factor Brandt has already applied (readme_wt.md:230 states 0.199*T_AB IS the installed-engine formula). The resulting L2 OEW agrees best with Wt!B12 of any option, which is the reason to reject it.

NOT like-for-like: this is the whole installed propulsion GROUP built item by item, while Brandt's B11 is one 0.199*T line and he books the inlet duct separately at B24. rows.parameter: [4b. THE TWO DEPENDENCY-INJECTED SCALARS -- both DEFINITIONAL by settled decision, not errors to chase]

rows.Notes: +43.9 %, ACCEPTED BY DECISION 2. Two deliberate, independent causes: (a) CONDITION -- a real cruise point from f16a_requirements.json vs Brandt's single stored SLS constant; (b) INSTALLATION BASIS -- get_TSFC returns the UNINSTALLED mil TSFC, Brandt's 0.70 is already installed (do not double-apply the 1.08). One consistency point in the framework's favour: Brandt's own Consts! cruise row is pct_AB = 0, i.e. dry/mil, and get_TSFC resolves to the mil path there -- the POWER SETTING matches. ! The Phase-3 claim that get_TSFC "duplicates" 0.70 was FALSE: it returns 0.70 at no condition (todo Sec. P4-15).

+44.1 %, and the two are DEFINITIONALLY different quantities: a design landing-weight rule of thumb vs a back-calculated subtotal of Brandt's OWN weight statement. Brandt's exact decomposition is W_TO - fuel - expendable stores = 31377.000000 - 6296.299422 - 4400 = 20680.700578, i.e. an implied ratio of 0.6591, not 0.95. ! THE 0.95 FACTOR HAS NO CITATION ANYWHERE IN THIS REPO -- user-supplied, todo Sec. P4-16 OPEN. It replaced a FROZEN W_l = 20681 that made the whole gear group insensitive to gross weight (Sec. P4-17).

rows.parameter: [5. NOT-MODELED GAP TALLY -- Brandt components with no framework analog at any fidelity level]

rows.Notes: 186.82 + 90.00 + 2016.86 + 440.00 = 2733.68 lbf = 13.68 % of Brandt Wt!B12. This is the single largest identified contributor to every OEW row's negative %Diff in section 1, and it is a MISSING-COMPONENT gap, not an equation error. Mirrors the geometry report's strake-gap treatment (todo 2026-07-25 Sec. 23).

rows.parameter: [6. SENSITIVITY TO THE ITEMS STILL OPEN AFTER THE 2026-07-25 DECISIONS -- Brandt = N/A, each applied ALONE on the settled L3 OEW base]

rows.Notes: A CITED geometry analog exists (geom.L_duct = 14.0 ft [Brandt Main!F32]) for what is currently an unpinned 7.5 ft estimate. Wiring it moves Eq. 15.10 air induction 227.54 -> 429.01 lbf (+88.5 %) and OEW by +201.47 lbf. Deliberately NOT wired this phase -- user decision required.

Same open question for the engine exit diameter: a cited geometry analog (geom.D_exit = 3.537022 ft, itself sqrt(T_AB_SLS/1900)) vs an unpinned ~40 in estimate. D_e enters Eqs. 15.10, 15.11 and 15.12, total OEW effect +24.94 lbf.

design_mach = 2.0 is BRANDT's Main! aircraft.Mmax [GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json:9]. The T.O. 1F-16A-1 operating Mach LIMIT is a DIFFERENT number, 2.05 [f16a_ground_truth.json:228]. Citing 2.0 to the T.O. would attribute a Brandt input to a primary document that says otherwise -- the same class of error as 19,148-cited-as-Wt!B12. The VALUE barely matters (+20.08 lbf on OEW via Eq. 10.10 M^0.25, Eq. 15.3 M^0.341 and Eq. 15.17 M^0.003), which is exactly why the citation must not drift unnoticed.

rows.Source: todo Sec. P4-11 (OPEN, unguarded by decision 6)
rows.Notes: ! THE ONLY PLACE THIS SILENT ZERO IS VISIBLE ANYWHERE. K_d = 0 is documented in WeightsL3.air_induction as the legitimate straight-duct value, and 0^0.182 = 0, so a legal documented input SILENTLY ZEROES the entire Eq. 15.10 air-induction component: 227.54 -> 0.0000 lbf, OEW 15705.33 -> 15477.79 (-227.54). No error, no warning, not even a NaN. NO GUARD IS ADDED, by explicit user decision 6, and there is deliberately NO unit test for this either -- testing unguarded behaviour would manufacture a false green. COROLLARY: if K_d = 0 is legal then the code's K_d cannot be Raymer's multiplicative base, because a straight duct does not weigh nothing, so the term's exponent or placement is itself suspect (todo Sec. 3a row 7). A guard alone would mask that.
